Afterwards, you will work back through the timeline and data to establish why it happened and what should change. Judge the seriousness of each event by its effect on services and people, then hand it to the engineering or site team best placed to fix it. Take command of high impact outages, running the bridge call, setting priorities for responding teams and recording each action against a timeline. Keep stakeholders informed with concise, accurate updates at every stage, from first alert to confirmed recovery. Follow facility events raised through the DCIM (Data Centre Infrastructure Management) platform, such as UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply), generator and cooling alarms, and stay with on site engineers until conditions are back to normal. Monitor external intelligence sources for weather, civil unrest and other risks to staff, travellers and facilities, confirm reports against a second source and start the agreed response, including police involvement where warranted. Review camera footage and door access records to look into unusual activity, and pass what you find to the relevant security team. Lead post incident reviews that establish what caused an event and recommend changes to stop it happening again. Keep every ticket accurate and complete, so each event carries a clear record of what happened and what was done. Work to documented procedures and agreed response times, and suggest improvements wherever gaps appear. Treat personal data such as video, access logs and travel details with care and in line with privacy law. Comfort working from documented procedures and against measured response targets. A calm, organised and decisive approach when several events are competing for attention.
